name: AXIA Energia
headline: Brazil's largest power generator, with a regulated high-voltage transmission network rivals cannot copy.
what_short: Brazil's largest power generator and grid operator
what_it_does: AXIA Energia is the largest electricity generator in Brazil, with 43,872 MW of capacity, much of it hydro. It also owns high-voltage transmission lines whose revenue is set by the regulator and indexed to inflation.
why_it_passed: The existing transmission network cannot be crossed by a rival with money, and the regulator sets the return it earns.
Transmission revenue is regulated and inflation-indexed, and the hydro fleet produces a known volume, so ten-year earnings can be pictured within a range.
The cash statements are clear and no dishonesty was found in management's record.
Its related-party contracts were reviewed and not found to show wrongdoing.
why_not_now: A regulator caps what its transmission business may earn, so the price is far above what that capped return justifies. At R$ 59.49 a share the expected return is only 3.6% to 5.1% a year in the central case, below both the 12.87% Brazilian government yield and the roughly 10% the analysis requires.
watch: The regulator is narrowing allowed returns, and its return on book equity averaged only 6.0% over 2021 to 2025.
The price of power from its hydro plants cannot be forecast, only bounded.
Value in US dollars depends on the Brazilian real, and Brazil's own interest rates are very high.
